text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a sudden spike of apiserver 503s and controller-manager reconcile lag in us-east1. Etcd WAL i/o spiked and watch queue backed up. Several GPU attach attempts from the provisioner started failing around the same time.
aj: Any logs? which apiserver instances?
maria: apiserver-prod-3 and etcd-1 hit heavy io. snippet from apiserver:
```
E0319 15:42:03.123 apiserver.go:123] 503 PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/default/configmaps/batch (10.8.3.45): apiserver received error from storage: etcdserver: request timed out
```
devops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: etcd-pod-1 WAL_IO=1.2GB/s, iowait=85% — autocreate-ticket #INC-4123
oliver: I see high NVMe latency on the node hosting etcd-1 (iostats show long avgq-sz). Could be transient cloud storage throttle.
tara: Also had a NAT SNAT exhaustion alert earlier in the hour for the region — lots of retries from nodes. Might explain attach failures.
aj: short-term: can we reduce watch fanout / increase apiserver client-side throttling? Pause non-critical controller work (batch job) and throttle the provisioner.
maria: did a quick canary: scaled down batch controllers in prod-ns and bumped etcd commit timeout to 10s; apiserver 503 rate dropped from ~8% -> ~0.6% in 7m.
sre-lead: Good mitigation. What's the root cause though? If this is recurring we'll need capacity changes or disk tiering.
maria: preliminary root cause: a ML batch job in prod created ~40k ConfigMap writes/min (model checkpointing metadata) — flooding API, writing small objects. Filing SRE-MLE infra ticket and will throttle writes at source. Assigned to @oliver and @aj to coordinate.
aj: follow-ups: 1) add WAL i/o alerts to paging, 2) add probe to provisioner to avoid rapid attach retries, 3) schedule a post-incident to discuss disk tiering vs compaction window.
maria: adding notes to INC-4123 and tagging ml-infra. leaving watch throttles in place for now. :thumbsup:
